slides.heading: Claude Code's Loop Skill
slides.body:
Your AI agent now works
while you're not watching.

Recurring tasks. Reminders. Monitoring.
All inside one session.

slides.heading: What is Loop?
slides.body:
A built-in Claude Code skill that
schedules recurring tasks for up to 3 days

Uses cron jobs under the hood
Works in Terminal, VS Code, and Desktop app

Invoke with /loop or just plain English

slides.heading: Two Modes of Loop

right_panel.title: One-Time Reminders
items: At 3 PM: remind me to call
In 45 min: stand up and stretch

slides.bottom_note: Both use cron jobs. One-time reminders auto-delete after firing.

slides.heading: How to Use It
slides.body: Just type naturally or use the /loop command:
slides.code:
# Using /loop command
> /loop 5m check if deploy is healthy

# Using natural language
> Every 10 minutes, check my ClickUp
  for new updates on our project

# One-time reminder
> At 3 PM remind me to review the PR

# Loop a skill
> Every 20 min run my review-pr skill

cards.title: Same Session Context
cards.desc:
Runs in your current session.
Reads previous context continuously.

cards.title: Loop Any Skill
cards.desc:
Chain with /review-pr, /commit,
or any custom skill on a timer.

cards.title: Natural Language
cards.desc:
No syntax to learn.
Just describe what you want.

cards.title: Cancel Anytime
cards.desc:
Just say 'stop the loop'
or 'cancel that reminder'.

slides.heading: How It Works Under the Hood
slides.body: Three cron tools power the entire loop system

slides.heading: 6 Ways to Use Loop Today
slides.body:
1. Monitor urgent emails every 5 min
2. Check deploy status every hour
3. Track a 3-day sprint deadline
4. Watch logs during testing
5. Run review-pr on a schedule
6. Build your own executive assistant

slides.heading: Know the Limits
slides.body:
3-day max expiry, then auto-deletes
Close terminal = all loops gone
No catch-up if you miss a fire
Each tab has its own separate loops

For anything longer than 3 days
use Scheduled Tasks instead
